title: Quibi: $1.75 billion and Hollywood's biggest names, shut down in six months

draft_outline: Quibi, launched April 6, 2020, shut down October 21, 2020, after 6 months. The company raised $1.75 billion, yet reportedly peaked at 500,000 paid subscribers.

Founded by Jeffrey Katzenberg and CEO Meg Whitman, Quibi aimed to deliver 'quick bite' video content, 10 minutes or less, for mobile users on the go. Investors like Disney and Alibaba contributed to its $1.75 billion funding.
Quibi's core strategy focused on high-production, mobile-only content accessed via a subscription model. A key decision was launching without TV casting capabilities and restricting content sharing.

This strategy met a changed user landscape: the April 2020 launch coincided with global lockdowns. Users were home, not commuting, and preferred watching on larger screens. The inability to share content hindered viral growth, and free short-form alternatives like TikTok already dominated the market.

By October 2020, Quibi ceased operations, 6 months after launch. Reports indicated subscriber numbers fell significantly short of projections. Much of its $1.75 billion capital was spent. Its content library was later sold to Roku for an estimated $100 million.
The Quibi case demonstrates that a large budget and established names do not guarantee success when product features and market timing conflict with user behavior.
